title: [Bug] PP>1 + spec decode: mamba align postprocess indexes block table by batch row of a stale (pp_size-old) batch -> recurrent state copied to wrong blocks (NaN / silent recall loss)
body:
## Summary

With pipeline parallelism (PP > 1) **and** speculative decoding (MTP / EAGLE-style proposer) on a hybrid Mamba/GDN model (`qwen4_exp` in our fork, but the code path is the generic mamba-align postprocess), the mamba "align" postprocess indexes the block table by **batch row** while the request↔row mapping it is given (`idx_mapping`) belongs to the batch from `pp_size` steps ago. When batch composition changes between those steps (a request finishes or a new one is admitted), the recurrent (GDN/conv) state is copied between the **wrong physical mamba blocks** — possibly a live neighbour's, or a block already freed and reassigned. Downstream the GDN recurrence / MoE produce NaN logits or silently wrong tokens.

Observed on 8×RTX 3090, TP=2 PP=4, `num_speculative_tokens=3`, 1M context with prefix caching: NaN logits in mixed 4-way concurrent runs (nan_lines=5 per run) and a measurable recall drop on a 945K-token RULER-style probe (12/20 and 14/20 correct vs 16/20 with speculation off). `SPEC=0` is unaffected (the align copy only runs on the spec-decode acceptance path); a single request never reorders, so single-stream tests do not trigger it; the fused vs non-fused draft loop only changes timing.

## Where

V2 GPU model runner (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py`): `execute_model()` starts with `update_pp_decode_requests()`, which pops the `PPHandler` FIFO entry from `pp_size` steps ago and passes its `idx_mapping` to `postprocess_sampled` → `MambaHybridModelState.postprocess_state` → `run_fused_postprocess_align`. The align kernel then used `batch_idx` to index the **gathered, batch-ordered** block table (whose contents are the T−1 batch's), i.e. rows from batch T−pp_size resolved against tables from batch T−1. Only ranks 0..pp−2 are affected (the last rank's mapping is current).

## Fix that worked for us

Index the align copies by **request slot** (`req_idx`, resolved through `idx_mapping`) into the request-ordered persistent block table (`BlockTables.block_tables[gid].gpu`) — the same `bt_row_idx = req_idx` convention `_copy_mamba_state_block` already uses — with the precopy synchronised accordingly. Zero extra cost. With the fix, the same mixed 4-way workload produced 0 NaN lines and the 945K recall returned to 15–16/20 (= speculation off). We also mask `-1` sentinel rows and rows past the live request count in the same path.

Reproducible on CPU with the real Triton kernel by constructing two consecutive batches with different request order (a request finishing between them) and checking which physical block the align copy touches; happy to share the test if useful.

## Environment

vLLM fork based on upstream ~`3f41d102` (0.26.1rc1 line), CUDA 13, Ampere sm86, V2 runner, cudagraph FULL_AND_PIECEWISE, MambaSpec block 1600 "align" mode, prefix caching on.
